title: Ignite 2026: Copilot is "the new OS for work," and now Office runs inside of it
content:
Opening the keynote at its Ignite event, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella outlined the company’s vision for its new “frontier ecosystem,” announcing Tuesday the general availability of Word, Excel, and PowerPoint inside Copilot, which he described as “the new OS for work.”
The announcement is a striking inversion of how we’ve traditionally used software. Rather than an app like Word being the attraction and Clippy the assistant to help you use it, Microsoft envisions the new Copilot integrations will see agents driving things, with the software packages riding shotgun. Applications will become plugin components of the agent’s work, backed by an organizational knowledge layer that draws context from emails, meetings, calendars, chats, and files. Users will now be able to create documents, spreadsheets, and presentations directly in Copilot, with the resulting files remaining editable in their respective Office applications.
The rollout marks a major step toward the Copilot redesign the company first announced in September. Parts of that vision are now becoming “generally available,” as Nadella puts it, with autonomous agents and new governance tools arriving alongside them.
All about agents
Copilot Autopilot (not to be confused with Windows Autopilot) is a “persistent, proactive agent for personal productivity” according to Microsoft. In a nutshell, Autopilot is a cloud-based autonomous AI agent that users can delegate responsibilities to, not just single tasks. Autopilot can be authorized to work across services like email and calendars and complete tasks assigned to it as part of its role. Autopilot will use usage-based billing via Copilot Credits, but final pricing has not been announced ahead of general availability.
Also announced as generally available at the keynote speech was Microsoft IQ, an intelligence platform that houses Work IQ, a context layer that helps agents understand a company’s communications, relationships, and ongoing work. Nadella described Work IQ as perhaps a company’s most valuable database: “It has a deep understanding of the people, their relationships to other people, your emails, your meetings, chats, projects that make up all the fabric of work.” Whether companies want autonomous agents to have access to internal documents and messaging data will have to be determined by their own internal IT review.

report.summary: At Ignite, Microsoft made Word, Excel, and PowerPoint generally available inside Copilot, positioning the agent—not the app—as the new OS for work.
report.background: For three decades, Office was the product and the assistant was a sideshow—Clippy being the cautionary tale. Microsoft's Copilot push since 2023 has been an attempt to invert that: first as a sidebar bolted onto Word and Excel, then, with the September redesign, as an agent-first surface where documents are outputs rather than destinations. The strategic logic is partly defensive. Google has been embedding Gemini throughout Workspace, OpenAI and Anthropic keep shipping agentic tooling that can draft documents without any traditional office suite at all, and the value of a productivity franchise shifts from per-seat licenses toward metered intelligence. Nadella's "frontier ecosystem" framing—agents plus a context layer plus governance—is Microsoft's bid to own the platform layer where enterprise work actually happens, rather than just the file formats. Ignite marks the point where parts of that vision move from preview to generally available, with usage-based billing and autonomous delegation arriving alongside.
key_points: The hierarchy is flipped: instead of a human opening Word and asking an assistant for help, agents now drive the work and Office apps become plug-in components they call. Users can generate documents, spreadsheets, and presentations inside Copilot, with the resulting files staying fully editable in the native applications.

Copilot Autopilot is a persistent, cloud-based agent that takes delegated responsibilities rather than one-off tasks. It can be authorized to operate across email and calendars over time. Microsoft will bill it on usage via Copilot Credits, though it has not published pricing ahead of general availability.

Microsoft IQ bundles Work IQ, a context layer that maps a company's people, relationships, emails, meetings, chats, and projects. Nadella calls it potentially the most valuable database a company owns—it is what lets agents understand ongoing work instead of guessing from a single prompt.

Governance ships alongside autonomy. Because agents may read internal documents and messaging, each organization has to run its own IT review to decide what Autopilot and Work IQ are permitted to see. Microsoft is positioning these controls as part of the pitch, not an afterthought.

The general availability of Office inside Copilot is the first concrete delivery from the redesign announced in September, signaling that Microsoft is converting demos into shipped, billable product ahead of rivals.
report.impact: For the AI industry, this is the clearest statement yet that the productivity battleground has moved from applications to agent runtimes and context layers—whoever owns the organizational knowledge graph owns the workflow. Expect Google, OpenAI, and enterprise startups to answer with their own context-store plus agent-delegation stories. For developers, the practical shift is toward building tools, connectors, and skills that agents invoke rather than UIs humans click; the MCP-style integration surface and permissioning become the new API design problem. For regular users, the near-term change is subtle but real: less app-switching, more delegation, and file formats that still open in Office. The bigger risks are metered costs that are hard to predict, agents acting on stale or wrong context, and a widening gap between organizations that have curated their Work IQ data and those that have not.
report.tools: To follow this closely, watch Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Studio (for building custom agents), and the Microsoft IQ / Work IQ documentation as it publishes. Competing stacks worth comparing: Google Workspace with Gemini, OpenAI's agent and enterprise offerings, and Anthropic's Claude with tool use. For open-source experimentation, try LibreOffice plus a local model via Ollama or Open WebUI, agent frameworks like LangGraph, CrewAI, or Letta (MemGPT) for persistent agents, and n8n for wiring email and calendar context yourself.
